audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is absent from both layers, and the entry's core advice runs directly against it. Riot's Lightslinger text: 'When Lucian is healed or shielded by an ally, or when a nearby enemy Champion is immobilized, his next 2 basic attacks will deal bonus magic damage.' Mel's Solar Snare roots. So Mel's own root arms two bonus-damage attacks for Lucian. The entry instead says 'Land Solar Snare's root to lock his E dash and guarantee a Radiant Volley follow-up' (wants.you[0]) and 'root him the instant he steps up or dashes in' (early).
audit.why: This inverts the advice. Rooting Lucian while standing inside his attack range does not lock him down, it powers him up - he eats the root, gets two empowered autos, and wins the trade he was losing. The root is still correct at maximum range, where the empowered attacks have nothing to hit. That distinction is the whole matchup and it appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: Root at max range, never beside him - immobilising him switches on Lightslinger's bonus damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells Mel to reflect two things Rebuttal cannot touch. dosFull[1].t is 'Reflect Relentless Pursuit back the moment he commits' - Relentless Pursuit is a dash, flagged dash only. And four separate strings describe reflecting 'his Lightslinger volley' (spikes[3], whys[5], mid) - Lightslinger is a passive attack empower, not a cast. The abilities actually carrying the projectile flag are Piercing Light (Q), Ardent Blaze (W) and The Culling (R).
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1 and it is Mel's only defensive layer. Holding it for a dash that will land regardless, or for an auto-attack buff, wastes the one cooldown that decides whether she survives his all-in. Naming the three real projectiles makes the hold a decision instead of a guess.
audit.corrected: Piercing Light, Ardent Blaze and The Culling are the three he throws.
audit.caveat: Medium not High on the ultimate specifically: whether a reflect catches The Culling is the same class of question as spell-shield eligibility, which the brief marks UNKNOWN and off-limits to assert from file data. Q and W are ordinary projectiles and safe. Worth a Wiki check before anyone states the R case more strongly than the wording I used.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] says 'Relentless Pursuit refreshes off his ability hits to close distance.' Riot's E text says the opposite mechanism: 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown.' It is his empowered ATTACKS that cut the dash cooldown, not his ability hits.
audit.why: It changes what you deny. If you believe abilities refresh the dash you space against his casts; in fact every empowered auto he lands on you or a minion brings the dash back sooner, so the thing to deny is his attack uptime. Base cooldown is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, which is long enough to matter if he is not attacking.
audit.corrected: Every Lightslinger attack he lands cuts Relentless Pursuit's cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no numbers, and breakdown.trading, tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and report[3].t all say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26.
audit.why: Same wrong number as the rest of this file, and it matters most in a matchup whose losing pattern is spending the barrier on chip. The useful numbers were also missing: Relentless Pursuit 16s at only 445 range, Piercing Light 9s at 500, The Culling 110/100/90 reaching 1400.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and ranges in breakdown.cooldowns; the 38s figure in breakdown.trading.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.phases[0] has side 'Lucian' while its own why reads 'Q volleys win every level-1 range war' - the label and the text contradict each other in the same object. phases[6].side is 'Lucian' while content.win[6] is 'Mel', and the matchup sits at 52.17% in Mel's favour.
audit.why: A reader looking at the chart is told Lucian owns levels 1 through 5 and the late game, while the prose beside it says Mel takes over from level 4 onward and the win rate agrees with the prose. The chart is the part that is wrong.
audit.corrected: NOT FIXABLE BY PROPOSAL: phases[N].side values are 3-7 characters and apply-proposals.js refuses any full-layer edit with a `before` under 12 chars. content.win[] already reads correctly, so nothing to change there. Flagged for a manual pass.

audit.why: I deliberately did NOT add anti-heal advice here even though _missing-interactions.json flags 'Lucian sustains through chip damage (Lightslinger (P)) - Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades'. That is a false positive: the heal flag on Lightslinger is derived from the phrase 'when Lucian is healed or shielded by an ally', which describes a trigger condition, not a heal he applies. Lucian has no self-sustain, and in a solo top lane there is no ally healer to trigger it either. Buying Grievous Wounds off that flag would be wasted gold.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Lucian if he plays it right. His Lightslinger passive double-shots after every ability, so a Piercing Light into auto out-trades your single Radiant Volley before you have the projectile count to commit. Your one window is Level 2: if you take Q + Solar Snare, you can root him the instant he steps up or dashes in and land a guaranteed Volley. Otherwise respect his range — don't walk into a Q-auto-auto trade you can't win, and save E for when he commits his Relentless Pursuit dash.

edits.before: This is where the lane swings to you. As Radiant Volley ranks up and Overwhelm stacks pile from repeated pokes, his short-range double-shot trades stop paying off. At 6, Golden Eclipse detonates every stack from any range, so even if he dashes to safety the burst still lands — bait his Relentless Pursuit, then root him with Solar Snare's orb and field once it's down. Rebuttal is your trump card: pop it as he commits his Lightslinger volley and you eat the burst, fire it back, and shield through his all-in.

notes: The headline find here is that Mel's own root feeds Lucian: Lightslinger empowers his next two basic attacks whenever a nearby enemy champion is immobilized, and Solar Snare is an immobilise. Both layers currently teach the reverse - 'land the root to lock his dash' - so this is the one matchup in my slice where following the existing advice actively loses the trade. The fix is a range qualifier rather than a ban: rooting at 1000 is still right, rooting at 500 is not.
